issue.body:
Check that the `variant` is non-null before attempting to decode the body, as it can be if the extending class sends requests before (indirectly) initializing the `variant`.

From logs in #8460.

body:
Nope, no such entries.

> $ grep -i extensionalert .ZAP_D/zap.log | wc -l
> 371
> $ grep -i attempting .ZAP_D/zap.log | wc -l
> 0

Reproduced the issue using Juice Shop application (running on the local host):

1. Navigate to Juice Shop landing page, using ZAP as proxy.
2. Remove any non-local hosts from Sites tree.
3. Run Active Scan with default settings.
4. Generate 'Risk and confidence HTML' report with default settings.
Can you persist/save the session zip it up and attach it here?
A reopened session does not reproduce the issue though.

Any progress here?

Or perhaps some tips of where I might look for the issue in the source code? I'm not familiar with ZAP's sources, but I'm willing to give it a shot to come up with a fix myself.
I'd suggest taking a look at the logic in `/reports/src/main/zapHomeFiles/reports/risk-confidence-html/report.html` and of the helper code.

Thanks.

After doing some debugging, I found that the issue was introduced with [e8e4b908d66fd17e4357dadf7836ba4c4a45a645](https://github.com/zaproxy/zap-extensions/commit/e8e4b908d66fd17e4357dadf7836ba4c4a45a645), and to be more exact [this line](https://github.com/zaproxy/zap-extensions/commit/e8e4b908d66fd17e4357dadf7836ba4c4a45a645#diff-29e4582c162294c68b87ef9e20a74f4fbb51541d89e976ea3938938e92efc668R449). Reverting the change on that particular line resolves the issue for me.

On said line, org.zaproxy.addon.reports.ReportHelper#getPortForSite() is used, with the full url passed into the method, e.g. http://juice-shop:3000/latest/meta-data/?EIO=4&transport=polling&t=P8uCTHA&sid=MqYjx2NC4PQnjZX9ACXZ.

Looking at the method's source code and unit test, it looks like it is only meant to handle urls up until the port number, not urls that contain a path. Yet an url with a path is passed, causing the method to return 80/443 for many urls that actually use another port. As a result, details for many/all of the alerts in my scan are not added to the report (my site uses a custom port).

Not sure if the change on this line can safely be reverted like this, but in any case, to me it looks like the getPortForSite() method should not be used in this way here. Or the method should be expanded to support urls with paths in them (I've created https://github.com/zaproxy/zap-extensions/pull/5772 for that, just in case).
